choice: Three-value palette (paper/ink/signal), one mono family with three sizes, five spacing steps, 640px measure. Hero size must be a clamp() and the hero number must not exceed four characters.
rationale: Direction A's coherence depends on scarcity: adding a fourth colour or second family dissolves the thesis.
The clamp and four-character rule convert the tournament's responsiveness finding into an auditable contract term rather than an assumption.
alternatives: Fixed 128px hero as originally described in Direction A — rejected because it fails at 375px.
Adding a sans family for prose — rejected as it contradicts the single-family thesis.
risks: The four-character rule is a design-time constraint with no mechanism to check it against real measured latency.
revisitWhen: a second surface needs a colour outside the three-value palette
